structuralViolations.constraint: §0B.13(2) — every AE-CAP key on AE_WIDGET_COMMIT_ALLOWLIST must be the `ae` side of exactly one AE_PROPOSE_PAIRING row, OR carry `propose: null` together with `confirmation_kind === 'APPROVAL'` — versus §0B.21, which allowlists crm.appointment.{attendance,duration,services,fields}.v1 with `confirmation_kind: 'BOOKING_CONFIRMATION'` and `kind: 'record'`.
structuralViolations.why: The three clauses cannot all be satisfied, and the conflict is not settled anywhere in Section 0, 0-B or Annex A. (a) §0B.11 is the published, normative propose↔AE mapping and states that a row appears 'only where that trace completed'; it has exactly 13 rows and none of them names any of the four. (b) No propose key for those four can exist: I enumerated MAYA_AI_TOOL_CATALOG (47 names) and the whole appointment family is appointments.own.{list,create,cancel,reschedule} — nothing for attendance, duration, services or fields; C9-CAP adds only the 9 non-appointment extras. (c) §0B.12 forbids filling a missing mapping 'by inference, by name similarity, or by a projector's choice at runtime', so the four rows cannot be invented, and FR-16 forbids adding a C9 key. (d) The `propose: null` escape is gated on `confirmation_kind === 'APPROVAL'`, which contradicts the BOOKING_CONFIRMATION the same clause assigns. Consequence: the §0B.13 assertion set fails at EP-REGISTRY-LOAD and the process does not start — the widget layer as specified is unbuildable, not merely reduced. This is fail-closed, so FR-6b still holds and no forbidden edge is constructible; but it is an unsatisfiable conflict between same-precedence normative clauses, and §0B.12 applies the OPPOSITE disposition to the structurally identical case (`expenses.delete` → GAP-EXPENSE-DELETE, reasoned as 'an AE capability with no propose key has no admissible DRAFT and therefore no admissible COMMIT under §0.34'). The correct resolution is to move all four to AE_CAPABILITY_GAP_LEDGER, not to relax §0B.13 — verified security colour: crm.appointment.attendance.v1, .duration.v1 and .fields.v1 carry NO `clientPrincipalTarget` (only create/reschedule/cancel/services do) while their `allowedActorRoles` is the permissive twelve-role TENANT_ACTION_ROLES default including CLIENT and CUSTOMER, and `resolveActorPermission` (action-engine.policy-resolver.ts:780–815) applies no target-ownership test on the actorUserId branch. Relaxing the pairing requirement instead would put a tenant-wide appointment mutation behind a client-role button. §0B.21 additionally allowlists `crm.appointment.attendance.v1` as a BOOKING_CONFIRMATION commit while Annex A P-21 forbids that act being presented to a client at all.

unprovenNormativeClaims: §0B.25 / §0B.28 FR-6e, second half: 'No capability satisfying TENANT_AUTHORITY is on AE_WIDGET_COMMIT_ALLOWLIST in this contract version … they are in AE_CAPABILITY_GAP_LEDGER under GAP-TENANT-ADMIN, no allowlist row.' This sentence names no enforcing mechanism and no evaluation point of its own, contrary to §S0.2 and to §0B.14's own polarity doctrine. §0B.16's start-up assertion set — the named mechanism for every other FR-6 family exclusion — contains explicit build-time vetoes for MONEY, BOOKING, MARKETING_FANOUT, CONSENT and IDENTITY, and contains NO line for TENANT_AUTHORITY; §0B.16's `row XOR gap` line forces classification but not which side a row lands on. P-23 (§0B.41) commissions 'the start-up assertion of §0B.16', which does not include this check, so the claim is not registered as NORMATIVE-PENDING either. Verified exposure: TENANT_AUTHORITY(cap) is satisfied by 28 of 226 capabilities, 14 of them ALLOW and reachable from `authenticated_request`, and 10 of those 14 carry the twelve-role TENANT_ACTION_ROLES default — including package5.wave2.claim-team-owner.execute.v1, .suspend-tenant.execute.v1, .create-tenant-user.execute.v1 and .update-tenant-configuration.execute.v1. Nothing in the contract's checked assertions would refuse such a row placed on the allowlist under family 'settings' or 'operational', where AE_FAMILY_FLOOR is the reachable SESSION_VERIFIED. FR-6e nonetheless HOLDS today: no allowlist exists (P-23 [ABSENT]), so no tenant-object capability has a button, and the cross-tenant half — TenantContextService.assertTenantId at Gate 4 plus evaluateTenantAccessState and assertNoCallerAuthority (action-engine.ingress.ts:161) — is [EXISTS] and bites. Remedy: one line in §0B.16, `row ⟹ TENANT_AUTHORITY(cap) ⟹ fail`.
verdicts.verdict:
NOT CERTIFIABLE — 1 structural, 0 security, 1 unproven (owner bar is 0/0/0). All fourteen fundamental rules HOLD; both findings are fail-closed and neither permits a forbidden edge to be constructed.

METHOD. I loaded the registries in-process rather than trusting transcription: ActionCapabilityRegistry.list() (226), canonicalProductionPolicyDefinitions() (221), MAYA_AI_TOOL_CATALOG (47), C9_CAPABILITIES (56). Every number Section 0-B publishes reproduces exactly — ALLOW 129 / SHADOW_ONLY 95 / DENY 2; 105 ALLOW+authenticated_request; 53 unreachable by allowedSourceTypes; MONEY 92 all / 39 reachable against the bare 'financial' token's 12 / 4; BOOKING 13 / 7; MARKETING_FANOUT 4; CONSENT 3; 98 distinct riskFacets tokens; 19 non-test approvalRequirement REQUIRED, all approverPolicyKey 'tenant-owner'; the seven-value autonomyLevel distribution; AE-CAP ∩ (C9-CAP ∪ TOOL-DEF) = ∅; 164/221 twelve-role default. I also confirmed the three load-bearing [EXISTS] claims by reading code: OWNER_HANDOFF has 0 occurrences under src/action-engine/ and that tree imports nothing from src/orchestration/ (EB-5 confirmed: the C9 `mode` is not a send fence); 0 of 221 policy definitions list 'authenticated_request' in trustedServiceSourceTypes (§0B.19(3)'s exclusion holds); BULK_ROOT_CAPABILITY is exactly communication.bulk-campaign.admit.v2.

THE RULES, EACH OVER ITS CORRECT KEY SPACE.
FR-1 HOLDS (closed effect router, only write edges = widget stores, three CONTROL handlers, CanonicalActionIngressService.prepare(); router [TO BUILD] under P-01, ingress-side assertNoCallerAuthority/assertResolverOwnsDecision verified at action-engine.ingress.ts:71,107,141,161).
FR-2 HOLDS (submission has no body/state member; widget_id 0 hits repo-wide; §0.50/§0.51 put frozen_nouns in AUDIT_RETAINED so no canonical decision reads CONVERSATION_CONTENT; load-bearing test is RT3(b) history-blind replay plus §0.52).
FR-3 HOLDS over AE-CAP. EB-3 is correct and I verified its premise: AE-CAP ∩ TOOL-DEF = ∅, so assertCanExecute(principal, AiToolDefinition) literally cannot be constructed for a COMMIT or REQUEST_APPROVAL — the old mechanism is VOID, not weak. The replacement, CanonicalActionPolicyResolver.resolve() → resolveActorPermission() over CanonicalActionPolicyDefinitionV1.allowedActorRoles + requiredFeatures + evaluateTenantAccessState against a Membership read inside the deciding request, is [EXISTS] (policy-resolver.ts:619, 748–772, 802) and total over AE-CAP minus the five kernel.test.* synthetics (221/226, verified). Honest and already-registered limit: that property is the permissive twelve-role default for 164/221 rows.
FR-4 HOLDS (EB-1's degenerate TOOL-DEF-over-AE-CAP term is replaced by the space-dispatched subjectFloor/aeFloor, total with named fail-closed defaults — including the `default:` arm over the untyped autonomyLevel, whose seven observed values I confirmed; ChannelProfile declares_verification_level: never).
FR-5 HOLDS (one fourteen-gate pipeline, single ingress; P-01 [ABSENT] so no shortcut exists; Gate 10's shadow status and missing promotion criterion are registered at §0.18-7 and P-20).
FR-6a HOLDS. NEVER_CHAT_ACTUATED is confirmed vacuous (all eight names and the identifier itself 0 hits), and the satisfiable replacement — CONSENT(cap) excluded from the allowlist — has exactly three members, of which the invalidation capability is additionally unreachable (allowedSourceTypes: ['legacy_bridge']) and record-client-consent.execute.v1 is fenced at the engine by actorPolicy VERIFIED_CLIENT_CHANNEL + assertConsentChannelBinding (verified). CONSENT_STATE is non-emittable today (P-09).
FR-6b HOLDS fail-closed (BOOKING := targetKind==='appointment'; §0.34's produced_by_intent_token_hash guard is unsatisfiable while P-18 is [ABSENT]) — but see the structural finding, which is inside this family.
FR-6c HOLDS, twice over. The real fence is communication.bulk-campaign.admit.v2's own AE properties — approvalRequirement REQUIRED, approverPolicyKey 'tenant-owner', allowedActorRoles exactly [tenant_owner, business_owner], actorPolicy REQUIRED, allowedSourceTypes ['authenticated_request'] — decided by ActionEngineKernel.decideApproval() against a live active Membership (kernel.ts:576–595, 1800–1815). All verified. The other three fanout capabilities are gap-keyed, and AE_FAMILY_FLOOR['marketing_fanout'] = STEP_UP_VERIFIED is unreachable while P-12 is [ABSENT].
FR-6d HOLDS by absence, honestly stated. The positive allowlist is the fence; MONEY is a veto only; no money-mutating capability is on the allowlist and PAYMENT_HANDOFF is gap-blocked with a null commit_intent (P-14). cash-declaration.* — ALLOW, widget-reachable, and carrying no money token of any shape — confirms that only a positive allowlist catches the family.
FR-6e HOLDS on both halves today, with the mechanism gap recorded above as the unproven claim.
FR-6f HOLDS as stated (role-gated approval, not separation of duties). EB-7 verified the same way as EB-3. The registered limits reproduce exactly: decideApproval never compares input.approverUserId to the execution's actor (self-approval, §0.49/§A4.1/§0B.27(1)), and controlledFixtureMode widens the approver set from two roles to six (kernel.ts:583–585, P-27).

WHY THE VERDICT IS STILL NEGATIVE. No actuating control exists anywhere in the system — the widget layer is [ABSENT] in full, P-23 admits nothing, and §0B.16 refuses to start a process over an unclassified registry. Under the bar's own reading that satisfies every conferral rule. What fails the bar is the artefact, not the fences: one pair of clauses in §0-B cannot both be satisfied and would halt the build rather than withhold a button, and one of the six family exclusions is asserted with no mechanism while the other five carry build-time vetoes. Both are one-line fixes — move crm.appointment.{attendance,duration,services,fields}.v1 to AE_CAPABILITY_GAP_LEDGER under a new GAP-APPOINTMENT-DETAIL-COMMIT key, and add `row ⟹ TENANT_AUTHORITY(cap) ⟹ fail` to §0B.16 — after which this lens returns 0/0/0 and CERTIFIABLE.

structuralViolations.constraint: §0B.29–§0B.31 declare `subjectFloor` dispatched by key space and total, with a named fail-closed default per branch; §0.13/§0.15 forbid a `undefined`-read path; §0.40 and §A1.2.1 both assert a non-empty emittable set that includes STRATEGY_OPTIONS, METRIC, CHART, PROGRESS and ARTIFACT.
structuralViolations.why: NOT CLOSED — 0-B voids the risk term for AE-CAP (EB-1) and re-enacts it verbatim for C9-CAP. §0B.31's `c9Floor` keeps `aiToolRegistry.get(key)?.riskTier ?? 'restricted'` with the comment `// valid: 47 of the 56 resolve`, which concedes 9 do not. VERIFIED in the canonical repo: `AiToolRegistryService` builds its map from `MAYA_AI_TOOL_CATALOG` alone (ai-tool-registry.service.ts:49-52) and `get()` (:58-73) THROWS `NotFoundException{ai_tool_not_found}` for any name outside it — it never returns undefined; and `c9.registry.ts:110-160` adds the 9 extras (`c7.measurement.read`, `c8.result.read`, `b35.preview`, `b35.status`, `b35.confirm`, `a22.configuration`, `owner_report.status`, `owner_report.download`, `c9.no_action`) OUTSIDE the catalogue map — 0 of the 9 are catalogue names. So `c9Floor` is total over 47 of 56 C9-CAP keys. Literal reading: the call throws, `verificationFloor()` is not total, and Gate 5 raises instead of returning a level — the exact defect EB-1 declares fatal. Charitable reading (wrap into a nullable): all 9 yield `'restricted'` ⇒ `RISK_FLOOR['restricted'] = STEP_UP_VERIFIED`, which §1.7 K6 / §0.18-5 / P-12 make permanently unreachable (verified absent at the substrate). Decisive consequence: `STRATEGY_OPTIONS`'s `no_action_option.select_intent` is MANDATORY, `priority: 0` and 'never dropped by degradation' (§2.6.11 STRATEGY.1), and its only owner-class key is `c9.no_action` (§2.4 row 11, §0.37) — one of the 9. Its floor is therefore a throw or an unreachable level, it is withheld at §4.5.4 step 1 with no `reachable_via`, and §4.5.5 C4 converts the emission into a LIMITATION/HANDOFF-only envelope. STRATEGY_OPTIONS is unemittable, contradicting §0.40 ('17 emittable') and §A1.2.1's corrected '16 emittable'. The same term permanently withholds every intent on `b35.preview/status/confirm` (CLIENT_LIST bulk, SETTINGS_DRAFT audience), `c7.measurement.read`/`c8.result.read` (METRIC, CHART), `owner_report.status/download` (PROGRESS, ARTIFACT) and `a22.configuration`.

structuralViolations.constraint: §0.34 states its purpose verbatim: `confirmation_of_ref` is generalised 'so cancel, reschedule and approval become mintable', with `kind: 'approval'` for an APPROVAL decision. §2 K11 (preserved unchanged by §0.16 E-31) names APPROVAL as one of exactly four COMMIT-bearing kinds. §0B.15 admits `confirmation_kind: 'APPROVAL'`; §0B.26 restates FR-6f in terms of an approve/reject intent being minted. §0.47 closes the list of reasons a decision intent may be null.
structuralViolations.why: NOT CLOSED, and 0-B restates the blocking clause. §0.34's guard reads: 'a COMMIT whose `confirmation_of_ref.kind !== "draft"` is mintable ONLY when `produced_by_intent_token_hash` is non-null and names a consumed REFINE/DRAFT record whose capability is the canonical owner's own propose key.' An APPROVAL decision has `kind: 'approval'` (≠ 'draft'), so the guard applies — but an approval object is created by a REQUEST_APPROVAL, not by a REFINE or a DRAFT: §3.2's effect table gives REQUEST_APPROVAL 'approval object only'; §2.4 row 12 gives APPROVAL the permitted effects NONE/NAVIGATE/COMMIT/HANDOFF, so it carries no REQUEST_APPROVAL of its own; and §3.11.1 says the decide intent points at 'the requesting IntentRecord', which is the REQUEST_APPROVAL record. A REQUEST_APPROVAL record is neither a REFINE nor a DRAFT, so the guard is unsatisfiable and BOTH decision intents are unmintable on every APPROVAL body. §0B.13(3) repeats the same REFINE/DRAFT-only condition, and §0B.13(2)'s `propose: null` allowance for 'the approval-decision case' makes it worse: a null propose side can never equal the capability of any consumed record, so (3) refuses unconditionally. The bulk-marketing path is the worked instance and is circular: §0B.22's sole allowlisted MARKETING_FANOUT row is `communication.bulk-campaign.admit.v2`, §0B.11 pairs it to propose key `b35.confirm`, and `b35.confirm` is one of the 9 C9 extras whose floor is itself unresolvable (violation 1). Finally §0.47 forbids the escape: it enumerates the ONLY reasons `approve_intent`/`reject_intent` may be null (state ≠ PENDING, TTL passed, `canDecide` false) and requires 'a fixture test asserts no other branch nulls a decision intent' — so the composer may not even null them for this reason.

structuralViolations.constraint: §4.5.4 fixes one normative ladder order: step 1 VERIFICATION FLOOR (withhold), steps 2–3 (withhold), step 4 PIN (protect `priority: 0`), step 5 FIT (drop). §0.17 confirms step 1 withholds and requires every withheld intent to be 'reachable via an emitted HANDOFF'; §4.5.5 C4 turns an unreachable withholding into a failed emission.
structuralViolations.why: NOT CLOSED by Section 0, Annex A or 0-B. Four normative clauses assert the opposite of step 1 for exactly the intents whose floor step 1 raises, and step 4's PIN runs too late to save them. (a) §2.6.15 SOURCE.3 is explicit and unambiguous: `reconnect_intent` is 'a HANDOFF whose target class is `s` … below that floor it is the only interactive element retained' — `targetFloor('s') = SESSION_VERIFIED` (§0.13), so below that floor step 1 WITHHOLDS the very intent SOURCE.3 says is retained. Two normative answers for one intent. (b) §2.6.16 SETTINGS.4 and §2.6.17 FORM.4/FORM.6 say `editor_handoff_intent` / `discard_intent` 'survives EVERY step of the degradation ladder'; the editor handoff is class `s`, floor SESSION_VERIFIED, withheld at step 1 on any channel capped below it (§1.7 K7 caps a polling Telegram bot at CHANNEL_IDENTITY), so a SETTINGS_DRAFT or FORM cannot be delivered there at all. (c) §0.25 / §3.12.6 make the escape verb 'never dropped by degradation' while `KIND_FLOOR` (§0.13) sets SESSION_VERIFIED for CONSENT_STATE, IDENTITY_BINDING, PAYMENT_HANDOFF, APPROVAL and CLIENT_LIST — so on those five kinds the mandatory escape is itself withheld at step 1 below SESSION_VERIFIED, and §4.8 A-5 ('the escape intent is always keyboard-reachable') and §4.7 V9 ('the escape verb is always live') cannot hold. The escape has no `reachable_via` by construction, so C4 fires. (d) §2.6.11 STRATEGY.1, as in violation 1. §0.17 preserves both halves and reconciles neither; the 'withhold' vs 'drop' vocabulary does not save (a), which says 'retained', or (b), which says 'every step'.

structuralViolations.constraint: §A2.4 (NORMATIVE): 'At `EP-REGISTRY-LOAD` the capability-gap ledger (P-07) is read and every `[ABSENT]` mechanism named in §A1 is bound to its gap key; a §A1 row with no gap key fails the start-up assertion and the process does not start.' §A2.5 offers that binding as the proof that a NORMATIVE-PENDING claim is checkable.
structuralViolations.why: CARRIED FORWARD, NOT CLOSED, AND WIDENED BY 0-B. §A1 has no gap-key column and names a gap key for no row. The ledger it points at (§0.37 + §0.38/§0.39) holds sixteen keys, every one of them an ACT with no canonical owner; not one corresponds to P-01 (gateway), P-02…P-06/P-08 (stores), P-10/P-11 (tables and a derivation), P-13…P-18 (facade, routes, handlers, a field) or P-19/P-20 (infrastructure). §0B.41 then adds SIX more rows — P-23 (`AE_WIDGET_COMMIT_ALLOWLIST`/`AE_CAPABILITY_GAP_LEDGER`), P-24 (`CapabilityRef`), P-25 (`AE_PROPOSE_PAIRING`), P-26 (Gate 6 dispatch), P-27 (`controlledFixtureMode`), P-28 (source-type discipline) — every one `[ABSENT]` and every one with no gap key, so the literal reading now fails for twenty-four of twenty-eight rows and the process never starts. The new gap keys 0-B does introduce (`GAP-TENANT-BILLING`, `GAP-COMMERCE-CREDENTIALS`, `GAP-VALUE-CONFIG`, `GAP-SUBSCRIPTION`, `GAP-REFERRAL-REWARD`, `GAP-CASH-DECLARATION`, `GAP-EXPENSE-COMMIT`, `GAP-EXPENSE-DELETE`, `GAP-BULK-SEND-DIRECT`, `GAP-TENANT-ADMIN`, `GAP-IDENTITY-SESSION`, `GAP-TENANT-CONFIG-COMMIT`) are AE-CAP CAPABILITY gaps keyed on `RegisteredActionCapabilityV1.capability`; none of them is a §A1-row binding, and §A2.3's four cited enforcing rules (§2 K20, §1.6.7 P2, §1.3 C5, §2.6.14 LIMIT.1) all key on a capability or a Cell having no OWNER, which an absent gateway, store, table or type is not. The fail-closed OUTCOME still holds for every row; the specific binding §A2.5 relies on to make the status checkable remains asserted rather than constructed, and is now less constructible than before.

structuralViolations.constraint: A normative clause must name a member that exists (§0.3: the three missing ROOT members are declared and 'every other root member is declared in §1 or §4'); §0.1 gives §3.1 sole ownership of `WidgetIntent`; §4.8 declares the accessibility floor 'normative and CI-gated'; one field carries one normative answer.
structuralViolations.why: CARRIED FORWARD, NOT CLOSED, AND A SECOND ANSWER ADDED BY 0-B. §4.8 A-2 (contract-v1.md:3202): 'Accessible name = `intent.utterance`, verbatim.' `WidgetIntent` (§3.1, :1500-1543) declares no member `utterance`; the members are `label`, `utterance_preview` and `speech_aliases`, and R3.1.2 says `utterance_preview` is a PREVIEW re-rendered at Gate 9 — so the two candidate referents are not equivalent and the named CI string check cannot be written. §0-B's errata (EB-1…EB-15) does not reach A-2, and §A2.8's NORMATIVE-PENDING marking repairs only the STATUS half — a NORMATIVE-PENDING rule is expressly 'binding on the implementation', so it still names a field the implementation cannot have. 0-B then adds a competing normative answer for the same control: §0B.36's new ARTIFACT row fixes 'accessible name = `filename` + `format` + `size_bytes`' for the kind's single tab stop (`fetch_intent`), while A-2 fixes it as `intent.utterance`, and §0B.35 simultaneously elevates §4.8.2 into the per-kind normative artefact. The pre-existing §4.8.2 APPROVAL row ('`audience_size`, `risk_tier` and reversibility appear in the approve control's accessible name') conflicts with A-2 identically, and is likewise untouched.

unprovenNormativeClaims: §0B.31's `c9Floor` comment `// valid: 47 of the 56 resolve`, offered as the warrant for retaining §0.13's risk term on the C9 branch. It is not a validity claim but a concession that 9 of 56 do not resolve, and 0-B states no default, no refusal and no gap key for them. VERIFIED: `AiToolRegistryService.get()` throws rather than returning a nullable (ai-tool-registry.service.ts:58-73), and none of the 9 C9-only extras is a catalogue name (c9.registry.ts:110-160 adds them outside the catalogue map). This is the unproven face of structural violation 1: the sentence reads as an assurance of totality over C9-CAP and is not one.

§2.6.5 BOOK.1 (contract-v1.md:956): 'ACTION ENGINE INGRESS independently re-derives the subject from the submitted capability and refuses when the emission's `confirmation_subject` disagrees.' §0.35 establishes verbatim from the code that `CanonicalActionIngressService.prepare()` receives `TrustedActionExecutionRequestV1`, which carries no widget-layer field, and that passing one would make a canonical mutation conditional on widget-layer state — which FR-1, FR-2 and E3 forbid. `confirmation_subject` is a widget body field, so the check is not constructible. §0.35 voids K11 and BOOK.2 and §0.16 E-18 voids BOOK.2, but BOOK.1 is named in no errata row of §0.16, no entry of §0.17, and no row of §0B.9; §A2.8 does not reach it (its evaluation point resolves to EP-CANONICAL, not EP-BUILD/EP-RENDER). Defence-in-depth left standing as normative. CARRIED FORWARD.

§4.7 V4 (contract-v1.md:3120-3122): 'the gateway refuses a `COMMIT` submission from a `SPOKEN` profile with no readback confirmation reference.' No such reference can exist anywhere in the contract as specified: §3.8's `WidgetIntentSubmission` is a closed shape with no member able to carry it and R3.8.2/§0.54 refuse unknown keys at any depth; `inputs` is unusable because §2 K12 fixes `commit_intent.input_schema === null` on all four confirmation kinds and Gate 8 refuses a submission carrying `inputs` for a null schema; §3.7's `IntentRecord` has no readback field; §3.9's fourteen gates contain no readback gate. §A1.1 P-01 marks the gateway absent, which is not the same defect — built exactly to this specification, the check still cannot be written. `SPOKEN` is the only non-RICH tier §4.5.3 permits to reach COMMIT ('up to COMMIT, readback mandatory'), so the stated fence on a spoken commit is asserted rather than enforced. 0-B does not reach it. CARRIED FORWARD.
verdicts.verdict:
NOT CERTIFIABLE — STRUCTURAL 5, SECURITY 0, UNPROVEN 3 (owner bar: 0/0/0).

WHAT SECTION 0-B CLOSES (7 of 7 named targets, all verified by re-executing the registries, not by grep):
1. Key-space misalignment — CLOSED. C9-CAP(56)/TOOL-DEF(47)/AE-CAP(226) are separated, AE-CAP ∩ (C9 ∪ TOOL) = ∅ confirmed, and every count in §§0B.3–0B.42 reproduces EXACTLY against `ActionCapabilityRegistry.list()`, `canonicalProductionPolicyDefinitions()`, `MAYA_AI_TOOL_CATALOG` and `c9.registry.ts`: 226 / ALLOW 129 / SHADOW_ONLY 95 / DENY 2; 105 ALLOW+`authenticated_request`; 53 unreachable by source type; `'financial'` 12→4; MONEY 92→39; 98 facet tokens; autonomy 19/95/1/50/42/14/5 with the single `L0_PROVIDER_DEFERRED` being the DENY'd `crm.visit.payment.v1`; 19 non-test REQUIRED all on `tenant-owner`; 221 policy defs with exactly the 5 `kernel.test.*` omissions; 164/221 on the twelve-role default; ZERO defs whose `trustedServiceSourceTypes` includes `authenticated_request` (§0B.19(3)'s load-bearing exclusion holds); `requiredConfirmationKind` 4/7/118 over 226 and 4/7/94 over 105 — §0B.33's indictment of the default branch is exact; CONSENT exactly 3; MARKETING_FANOUT exactly 4 with the stated roles/approval; `MONEY ∩ BOOKING` = {`crm.visit.payment.v1`}, DENY, so §0B.16's vetoes do not collide on any of the 7 booking rows.
2. Floor's undefined risk domain — CLOSED FOR AE-CAP (`aeFloor`: four explicit fail-closed returns plus a `default` for the untyped `autonomyLevel`), NOT for the 9 C9-only extras → structural violation 1.
3. RoleHint 12-vs-11 — CLOSED (§0B.34 / EB-10: one union, declared once, referenced by name).
4. §4.8.2's 17-row floor table — CLOSED (§0B.36 / EB-13: 22 rows, the five new ones consistent with §2.4's `role_hint`).
5. Double `kindCeiling` — CLOSED (§0B.37 / EB-14: 90 s and 120 s, the shorter values, per L3 and RT4).
6. Incomplete `on_expiry` — CLOSED (§0B.37 / EB-15: 22 rows; `re_resolve` for all five omitted kinds is reached by one rule, not five judgements).
7. SETTINGS_DRAFT vs expenses — CLOSED (§0B.38-39 / EB-9). Verified: `expenses.create.execute.v1` = `['local','financial','expense_ledger','atomic']`, ALLOW, approvalRequirement REQUIRED, `targetKind: 'expense'` — MONEY by three independent terms, exactly as §0B.39 states. The honest capability reduction of §0B.40 is stated rather than hidden.

FUNDAMENTAL RULES: HOLD, fail-closed. FR-3/6a/6c/6d/6f each had a VOID mechanism before 0-B; each now names a mechanism that either is `[EXISTS]` and verified in the dumps (`CanonicalActionPolicyResolver.resolve()` over `allowedActorRoles`+live Membership; `actorPolicy: 'VERIFIED_CLIENT_CHANNEL'` + `assertConsentChannelBinding`; `communication.bulk-campaign.admit.v2`'s owner-only REQUIRED approval; `decideApproval` → `CANONICAL_APPROVER_POLICY_ROLES`) or fails closed by absence (P-23 absent ⇒ §0B.33 refuses every COMMIT mint ⇒ no actuating control exists today).
